notes:
I couldn't write these notes because the research didn't work. My first attempt to fetch the pages crashed because of a bug in my code, and when I went to retry, the tool told me I had no more uses left for this turn. I never got content from any source, so I have nothing I can attribute to a page.

You asked me to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. If I wrote the notes now, I'd be filling them in from memory, which breaks that rule. So there are no notes below.

These are the pages I was trying to read first. If you ask again, I'll start with them:

- **Verse-by-verse, traditional reading:**
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-148/
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/148.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/148.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/148.htm
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/psalm-148-commentary
- **Modern scholarship:** NET Bible notes at https://netbible.org/bible/Psalms+148, which should cover the "waters above the skies" in v. 4 and the "horn" in v. 14.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's exposition of Psalm 148 at https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1801148.htm.
- **Other Protestant traditions, still to search:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (Baptist), Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu (Methodist), and Lutheran and charismatic sources. These would show whether the traditions really disagree anywhere. On v. 14, "a horn for His people" may or may not be read as pointing to Christ.
